title: Delete Duplicate Folders in System
summary: Given a 2D array paths, where each element represents an absolute path to a folder in the file system, identify and mark all folders that are identical to at least one other folder, including their subfolders.
statement: Given a 2D array paths, where each element represents an absolute path to a folder in the file system, identify and mark all folders that are identical to at least one other folder, including their subfolders. Once marked, delete these folders and their subfolders, but do not delete folders that become identical after the initial deletion. Return the paths of the remaining folders in any order.
constraints: paths contains 1 through 20000 distinct absolute folder paths, and every non-root folder's parent is included.
Folder names have 1 through 10 lowercase letters; total name characters are at most 200000.
Two nonempty folders are duplicates when their complete nonempty child-name/subtree structures match; mark once, delete marked folders and descendants, and return remaining paths in any order.
hints: A folder's complete structure has a canonical bottom-up signature made from each child name paired with that child's signature.
Build a trie, count every nonempty subtree signature, then traverse again while skipping roots whose signature count exceeds one.
encode children in sorted-name order; count nonempty encodings; collect paths unless the child's encoding is duplicated.
Equal canonical signatures are equivalent exactly when all named descendants match recursively. Counting precedes deletion, so folders made equal only afterward are correctly retained.
editorial: Equal canonical signatures are equivalent exactly when all named descendants match recursively. Counting precedes deletion, so folders made equal only afterward are correctly retained.

tests.explanation: Folders a and c both contain only an empty b folder, so both subtrees are removed and d with d/a remains.
The b subtrees differ because only a/b/x has child y, so no folder is deleted.
